chunks: A group narrated to me, from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa, from Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi, who said: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Saad al-Qummi narrated to us, saying: I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) on one of the days and said: O my master, I am absent and present, but it does not become easy for me to reach you whenever I am present. Whose word should we accept? And whose order should we obey?

He (peace be upon him) said to me: This is Abu Amr, the trustworthy and honest one. Whatever he says to you, he says it from us; and whatever he delivers to you, he delivers it from us. When Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) passed away, I reached Abu Muhammad, his son al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him), on a certain day and said to him (peace be upon him) what I had said to his father. He said to me: This is Abu Amr, the trustworthy and honest one, the trustworthy man of the past and my trust in life and death. Whatever he says to you, he says it from us; and whatever he delivers to you, he delivers it from us. Abu Muhammad Harun said: Abu Ali said: Abu al-Abbas al-Himyari said: We would often discuss this statement and describe the eminence of the status of Abu Amr.

key_terms.الثقة الأمين: The Trustworthy and Honest (title for the special emissary)
key_terms.ثقة الماضي: The trustworthy man of the past (referring to the predecessor Imam's trust)
key_terms.ثقتي في المحي والممات: My trust in life and death (referring to the current Imam's ongoing trust)
key_terms.فَعَنِّي يَقُولُهُ: He says it from us (indicating the emissary's speech carries the Imam's authority)

ai.seo_question: Who was the trusted representative of the Imams during the Occultation and how was his authority verified?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the institutionalized trust (*thiqa*) placed in Abu Amr during the Minor Occultation, serving as a critical precedent for the later concept of *marja'iyya* in Shia jurisprudence. The dual confirmation by both Imam al-Hadi and Imam al-Hasan al-Askari highlights the continuity of divine authority through a single, verified representative, ensuring that the community’s religious obligations remained anchored in the Imam’s presence despite his physical absence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 315 - A group of scholars narrated to me from Abu Muhammad Harun Ibn Musa from Abu Ali Muhammad Ibn Himam Iskafi that he said: Narrated to us Abdullah Ibn Ja’far Himyari that: Narrated to us Ahmad Ibn Ishaq Ibn Saad Qummi that: On a certain day, I came to Abul Hasan Ali Ibn Muhammad (a.s) and said: “O my master, many a time I go away and then come to your vicinity, yet I am still not able to get access to you every time I come. So whose word should we accept and whose order should we obey?”

The Imam (a.s) said: “This is Abu Amr. He is trustworthy and honest. He is the trustworthy man of the past and my man of trust in my lifetime and after my death. Whatever he says to you, he says it from us; whatever he delivers to you, he does so from us.” When Imam Hadi (a.s) passed away and the Imamate was transferred to his son, Imam Hasan Askari (a.s), I came to him one day and mentioned what his respected father had said. Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) also said: “This is Abu Amr. He is trustworthy and honest. He is the trustworthy man of the past and my man of trust in my lifetime and after my death. Whatever he says to you, he says it from us; whatever he delivers to you, he does so from us.” Abu Muhammad Harun said: Abu Ali said: Abul Abbas Himyari said: We would often discuss this narration and extol the eminence of Abu Amr.
